SOX.source: Polygon I:SOX daily bars, re-fetched this run. The leadership was memory and storage rather than AI accelerators: NVIDIA added only 0.84% and Broadcom 0.21%, so the cap-weighted contribution of the two largest names cannot account for a 3.4% index move. On the week the index is +2.316% from 11469.66. NOT ATH, and not close - even after Friday's 3.4% session the index is -19.81% below its record close of 14634.72 set 6/22/26 and -19.93% below the 14655.29 record high from the same session. A one-day move of Friday's size closes roughly a sixth of that gap.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Polygon I:VIX daily bars, re-fetched this run. Up 1.467% Friday to 14.53 and essentially unchanged on the week from 14.43 on 8/28. This is the most informative number on the board precisely because it did nothing. A payrolls print that beat consensus by more than a hundred thousand jobs, repriced the September FOMC meeting toward a HIKE, and knocked the S&P 500 lower moved implied volatility by two tenths of a point and left it in the low 14s. Companion VXN fell to 20.04 from 20.16, also re-fetched. Options markets are not pricing the September meeting as a risk event, which is either complacency or a well-founded read that the outcome is already conditional on a CPI print that has not happened yet.

US2Y.label: US 2Y Yield
US2Y.source: Treasury par yield curve CMT, re-read this run from the home.treasury.gov daily CSV. The 2-year rose three basis points Friday to 4.37% against the 10-year's one, taking the 2s10s spread to 41bp from 43bp - a BEAR FLATTENING, which is the textbook shape for a market marking up the near-term policy path while leaving its terminal view broadly intact. On the week the 2-year is also +3bp from 4.34%, and the curve is two basis points STEEPER week-over-week at 41bp versus 39bp, so the flattening is a Friday event rather than a weekly trend. The 2-year traded as high as 4.416% intraday, its highest since January 2025. GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: GCUSD front-month settle, timestamp 2026-09-04 21:00:00 UTC, verified this run. Down 1.394% Friday to $4476.60, the largest single-day decline on the board. The mechanism is straightforward and worth explaining to clients who expect gold to rise on Middle East escalation: a strong payrolls print raised real yields and the odds of a rate HIKE, and gold pays no coupon, so a higher real discount rate is a direct headwind regardless of the geopolitical backdrop. Silver fell in sympathy, 1.41% to $66.75, and the dollar index rose 0.25% to 99.16. On Friday, rates beat geopolitics.

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: Polygon C:AUDJPY daily bars, re-fetched this run. Up 0.413% Friday to 112.52. The classic risk-appetite carry proxy, and the read matters for the week's central interpretive question: was last week's 2.4% yen surge a disorderly carry unwind or an orderly repricing of Bank of Japan policy? AUD/JPY rising on Friday, alongside VXN FALLING to 20.04, says orderly repricing. A genuine carry unwind takes this pair sharply lower and drives implied volatility higher; neither happened. USD/JPY settled 156.246, having fallen 2.384% on the week almost entirely in the single Wednesday-to-Thursday move from 158.893 to 155.641 - a Bank of Japan story ahead of its September 17-18 meeting, not a global risk event.
